questions.stem: A 22-year-old man attended clinic for review of a splitskin graft to a full-thickness burn on his left calf. The doctor was concerned about infection as there was worsening exudate and pain, with 2 cm erythema around the edges. A wound swab was taken, and the patient started on empirical flucloxacillin. Wound swab: 1. Staphylococcus aureus, sensitive to methicillin 2. Streptococcus pyogenes 3. Gram-positive rod, identifying as Corynebacterium diphtheriae, awaiting confirmation
questions.lead_in: What confirmatory test on organism 3 would substantially alter the management of this patient?
questions.explanation: Modified Elek test The Elek immunoprecipitation test confirms the production of diphtheria toxin. PCR tests are now also available to demonstrate presence of the diphtheria toxin genes. Diphtheria toxin production requires enhanced public health management of both the patient and their close contacts.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 8 Q50

questions.question: [image-based question: picture of throat (white/grey plaque in posterior oropharynx); picture of media with black colonies]

parts.text: What is the name of the plate used to workup the organism?

cohort_answer.text: Diagnosis: diphtheria. Plate used to workup the organism: Tinsdale.

questions.question: Girl, fully vaccinated, admitted for femur fracture. Brother admitted with diphtheria pharyngitis. Girl has c. diphtheria in throat swab, asymptomatic and has no wounds.

parts.text: What precautions to put her on
When can you safely d/c her precautions
How would you manage this patient – be specific regarding abx and whatever else you’d do

cohort_answer.text: When abx therapy is complete and 2 throat swab (or skin swab if lesion) cultures are negative x 2 24hrs apart.

questions.question: A 30-year-old woman is admitted for a hip fracture. Her son at home has pharyngitis and is diagnosed with Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection. She is asymptomatic, but a screening swab is done and is positive for C. diphtheriae – (2019)

parts.text: What infection control precautions are required, if any?
What criteria are required to discontinue infection control precautions?
What are TWO aspects of management (list specific drug[s], if applicable).

cohort_answer.text: Precautions: Droplet/Contact (+ Standard). Discontinue when: two consecutive cultures (separated by 24 hours) are negative. Management: antimicrobial prophylaxis - Erythromycin 250mg PO QID x7-10 days OR Penicillin G Benzathine 1.2MU IM x1 dose; assess vaccination status and update if incomplete and/or last booster not within past 5 years.

parts.text: C) What is the main virulence factor and its mechanism?

cohort_answer.text:
Isolation (routine practices + droplet precautions for pharyngeal, or contact for cutaneous) until proof of elimination of C. diphtheriae; Report to public health. Proof of elimination: 2 consecutive negative cultures 24h apart, 24h after cessation of antibiotics. Other measures: review vaccination, NP swab cultures, immediate diphtheria toxoid dose, Pen G benzathine IM x1 for exposures (or erythromycin x7-10 days)
Tox+ strains: potent exotoxin inhibiting protein synthesis in mammals (ADP ribosylase A domain + binding B domain). Toxic effects on heart, nerves, kidneys causing myocarditis, delayed peripheral nerve conduction, ATN
